entities.name: Parvovirus B19
observations: B19 DNA has been detected in benign/normal testicular tissue and in testicular germ-cell tumour specimens, but detection is inconsistent and does not establish causation.
Microdissection found B19 sequences across tumour and non-tumour compartments in one mixed tumour, arguing against tumour-cell restriction.

entities.name: Benign testis
observations: B19 PCR was positive in 4/10 testes with benign histology in a 1999 study.
B19 capsid proteins were reported in 6/7 normal testicular samples in a 2012 study, although detailed controls and localization were not provided.

entities.name: Testicular germ-cell tumour
observations: B19 DNA has been reported in seminoma-containing and other germ-cell tumour specimens, with frequencies ranging from 3/36 (8.3%) to 33/39 (85%) across studies.
A 2019 systematic review/meta-analysis found no significant association between B19 infection and testicular carcinogenesis.

entities.name: B19 tissue detection
observations: B19 tissue detection occurs in both benign/normal testis and testicular germ-cell tumours, but tissue presence should not be equated with disease association or causation.

entities.name: No causal association
observations: Prediagnostic serology showed no increased testicular cancer risk (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.60–1.77), and pooled evidence did not support B19-driven testicular carcinogenesis.
Very low viral loads in a replication study were compatible with persistence or latency rather than established active oncogenesis.
